finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL. Its only check is a substring match for "example.io" anywhere in the string. The server fetches the URL, follows redirects (default client), and returns the body to the caller. This is a full-read SSRF.
finding.source: HTTP request parameter `logo` via r.FormValue (main.go:31), controlled by any unauthenticated client of the /logo endpoint
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response body copied to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: /logo route registered on the public listener :8081

strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only validation. It does not parse the URL or check the host or scheme, so it passes for http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://127.0.0.1:8081/?example.io, or http://example.io.evil.com/
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects, so a redirect from an attacker host also reaches internal targets
The response body is returned to the attacker, so internal data is exfiltrated. The error from http.Get is also ignored, so a failed fetch causes a nil dereference panic.

finding.guards_checked: Substring check on the raw string (main.go:32) is bypassable via query string, path, fragment, userinfo (http://example.io@evil/) or subdomain. There is no scheme or host allowlist, no private/link-local IP blocking, and redirects are not restricted. No authentication.

verdict.guard_found: Only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32 (substring check, not a closing guard). The strict trusted-host map and no-redirect client exist only in the separate /cdn handler (main.go:10-25) and are not applied to /logo.
verdict.reason: r.FormValue("logo") (main.go:31) passes only the substring check at main.go:32, then reaches http.Get(raw) at main.go:36 with the default redirect-following client, and the body is copied to the caller at main.go:38; there is no auth, so any client can trigger the SSRF. The finding's line-42 trace note is slightly off, since /logo is registered at line 43, but this doesn't change the verdict.
